newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Ireland launches 5-step guide on preparing for EMU.
newsitem.headline: Ireland launches 5-step guide on preparing for EMU.

text.p: Irish industrial development agency Forfas launched a five-step guideline for Irish firms to help them manage the changeover to European economic and monetary union (EMU).
The guideline, which was devised by consultants Arthur Andersen, is part of the government's EMU business awareness campaign and was launched at a conference on the changeover to the euro on Monday.

Forfas said that businesses, whether they employed 20 or 2,000 people, should ensure that they were fully prepared for the changeover to the single currency which is scheduled for introduction on January 1, 1999.

"A lot has been said and written about EMU in recent months but there remains a significant danger that Irish firms will under-estimate the time and effort involved in preparing for EMU," Forfas chief executive John Travers said.
He said there were clear advantages to be gained by firms in completing the initial planning steps as early as possible.
"Companies which put off taking action until 1998 or later may well find that any decision to delay preparation has proven to be a costly one," Travers said.
The five steps involved in the guideline are:
-- the assignation of responsibility and the gathering of information
-- the identification of the functional implications for business
-- the preparation of a functional work plan
-- the design, testing and implementation of the changes required.
